title: Outbound: how is a draft claimed so a double click can't send it twice?
scope: The owner's Send click, the sendAction server action, and the atomic UPDATE…RETURNING claim in Postgres.
omissions: Guard checks, Gmail/LinkedIn delivery and reply detection after claim
Drafting, enrollment, cron jobs and the LinkedIn browser worker

nodes.label: Web browser
nodes.description: Today or conversation view; Send button

notes.title: Atomic claim
notes.text: One UPDATE sets status 'sending' and saves any edited body/subject, WHERE id matches, direction 'out', status in draft/failed. No returned row → skipped: 'Already sent or no longer a draft.'

notes.title: Suppression, not exactly-once
notes.text: The claim stops a second click or tab from sending. Later guards reset the row to failed (no person, daily limit) or skipped (closed stage, already replied). Delivery is not guaranteed.

notes.title: Crash after claim
notes.text: A row stuck in 'sending' can't be claimed again; only draft/failed rows qualify. The health check flags LinkedIn rows stuck over 3h. The code shows no automatic recovery for email.
